contributions.item_title_en: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care: Update on winter preparedness
contributions.text_english:
Year after year, the previous Government failed to prepare sufficiently for the winter months. In May, the people of Wales put their faith in this Plaid Cymru Government to prioritise our NHS. And I welcome the statement today, which is breaking the cycle of waiting for winter to arrive before reaching it.

Many of the priorities set out in the statement can only succeed through local implementation. Could the Cabinet Minister please provide more detail on how the Government will support those providing healthcare in our communities? They are often under-resourced and under immense pressure, but if we can get this right, it would reduce the pressure on A&E, keeping people in their communities and out of hospital, where there is a chance they would pick up further illness and infection. Diolch.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
contributions.text_english: The Welsh Government has just announced a package of almost £5 million to support those experiencing poverty and to build financial resilience in the long term across our communities. How will the Government ensure that this funding reaches the most vulnerable, particularly in rural parts of our constituency of Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd? Thank you.
contributions.text_original: Mae Llywodraeth Cymru newydd gyhoeddi pecyn o bron i £5 miliwn i gefnogi'r rhai sy'n dioddef tlodi ac i adeiladu gwydnwch ariannol hirdymor ar draws ein cymunedau. Sut fydd y Llywodraeth yn sicrhau bod y cyllid hwn yn cyrraedd y rhai mwyaf bregus, yn enwedig mewn rhannau gwledig o'n hetholaeth ni, Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd? Diolch yn fawr.

contributions.item_title_en: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
contributions.text_english: I know that many Members were at the NFU reception last week, and hearing the union and farmers thank the Minister for a number of decisions this Welsh Government has taken so far to support them speaks volumes. For the first time, farmers feel heard. Plaid Cymru's manifesto commits to rural-proofing our communities, including those in my constituency of Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd. Could we have some information on the progress of the rural development strategy for Wales and how this will tackle poverty and create new economic and social opportunities for my constituents?

contributions.item_title_en: 4. 90-second Statements
contributions.text_english: Yesterday marked World Heart Day, a day that brings together a global community to raise awareness of cardiovascular disease, one of the most significant health challenges we face. CVD is responsible for more than one in four deaths in Wales, and Public Health Wales projects a 46 per cent increase in heart failure by 2035. These figures are stark, and they remind us why continued action, investment and awareness are so essential. I want to extend my thanks to the British Heart Foundation for bringing the red bench to the Senedd steps yesterday. It served not only as a symbol of remembrance, but also as a powerful prompt for conversation about prevention, early diagnosis and support. I'm grateful to all Members who took the time to visit the bench and showed their commitment to improving heart health across our communities. I also want to place on record my appreciation for the many individuals, clinicians, researchers, volunteers and organisations across Wales who work tirelessly to prevent cardiovascular disease, improve care pathways and strengthen the data we rely on to deliver better outcomes. Their dedication ensures that no matter where people live in Wales they can access the support and treatment they need. Together, we can continue to raise awareness, promote healthier lifestyles, and push for the improvements that will save lives for generations to come.

What other opportunities are there alongside this project that will help people in my constituency? Diolch.

contributions.item_title_en: 2. Business Statement and Announcement
contributions.text_english: Prynhawn da, Weinidog. Can I thank the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability for the statement he issued during recess on the issue I raised previously regarding pollution in the River Tawe? Constituents continue to contact me, raising concerns regarding the need to tackle pollution in our rivers, seas and lakes. I would therefore be grateful if the Minister would provide us with an update on the creation of the new Welsh water regulator, in giving Wales greater control over how our water and natural resources are managed and regulated. contributions.item_title_en: 3. Statement by the First Minister: Weather, wildfires, drought and resilience
contributions.text_english: Thank you, First Minister, for this important statement.
contributions.text_original: Diolch, Brif Weinidog, am y datganiad pwysig yma.

contributions.item_title_en: 3. Statement by the First Minister: Weather, wildfires, drought and resilience
contributions.text_english:
It really is unbelievable seeing the party opposite continue to deny the cause of this issue affecting our rural communities. I believe a big part of being a politician is actually listening to what's being said, and I really wish Members had done that today.

Having recently met with a farmer in the Llangynidr area of my constituency seriously impacted by the recent wildfires, he spoke about the fact that Welsh Water infrastructure was unmaintained and hindered efforts to tackle the fires. Can we have assurances that the Welsh Government will put pressure on agencies like Welsh Water to ensure the inspection, clearance and ongoing maintenance of their infrastructure, especially across rural parts of the country that have been impacted so much by the wildfires? Diolch.

contributions.item_title_en: 4. 90-second Statements
contributions.text_english: Diolch, Lywydd. Gaynor Hopkins was born on 8 June 1951 in Skewen, Neath, one of six children to her father, Glyndwr Hopkins, a coal miner, and her mother, Elsie Hopkins. From humble beginnings, she became known all over the world for her distinctive raspy voice, immense emotional range and timeless anthems. Yes, Bonnie Tyler was a legend. With her well-known hits such as 'Total Eclipse of the Heart' and 'Holding Out for a Hero', Bonnie Tyler went on to sell millions of records all over the world. Not just a singer, Bonnie was an ambassador for many charities and used her global profile to champion them, supporting events and making appearances at charitable functions. Once saying, 'I'm just a girl from a small town in Wales who just loves to sing', she never forgot her Skewen roots. Sadly, on 9 July 2026, at the age of 75, we heard of the singer's passing. Our thoughts are with her family, friends and all those affected by her death.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the First Minister
contributions.text_english: Thank you, First Minister. The additional funding is a great opportunity to make a difference and to start to implement the priorities of the people of Wales. The funding is focused on activities that can be implemented in this financial year, including direct funding for schools to stabilise and support the current provision and to enable a sustainable long-term approach. I fear that stopping this additional funding will put that at risk, will keep the sectors in a very difficult position and will go against the priorities that the people of Wales voted for this year. Despite this, it's clear that ALN support is needed in Wales. So, how will this Government work in a meaningful and effective way to support the sector?
contributions.text_original: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Mae'r cyllid atodol yn gyfle mawr i wneud gwahaniaethau a dechrau gweithredu ar flaenoriaethau pobl Cymru. Mae'r cyllid yn ffocysu ar weithgareddau sy'n medru cael eu gweithredu yn y flwyddyn gyllidol hon, gan gynnwys cyllid uniongyrchol i ysgolion i sefydlogi a chefnogi'r ddarpariaeth bresennol ac sy'n galluogi dull cynaliadwy tymor hir i ddod i'r amlwg. Rwy'n ofni y bydd atal y cyllid atodol hwn yn peryglu hynny, yn cadw'r sectorau mewn sefyllfa hynod o anodd ac yn mynd yn erbyn y blaenoriaethau fe bleidleisiodd pobl Cymru drostyn nhw eleni. Er hyn, mae'n amlwg bod angen cymorth ADY arnom yma yng Nghymru. Felly, sut fydd y Llywodraeth hon yn mynd ati mewn ffordd ystyrlon ac effeithiol i gefnogi'r sector?

contributions.item_title_en: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy: New Development Agency for Wales
contributions.text_english: It's a very strange tactic from the opposition, I'd say—criticising this Government for having plans when they have none.
contributions.text_original: It's a very strange tactic from the opposition, I'd say—criticising this Government for having plans when they have none.

contributions.item_title_en: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy: New Development Agency for Wales
contributions.text_english: I'm sure that everyone in this Chamber wants to see brand Wales succeeding. For this to happen, we need to help Welsh businesses to grow, to innovate, and to trade internationally. We need to attract inward investment and to increase the number of sustainable, high-quality jobs that pay well. We know that the previous business landscape was piecemeal and was often confused, meaning that businesses did not receive the support that they needed when they needed it. So, we welcome this step of creating a national development agency for Wales as a one-stop hub to support businesses of all kinds across the nation. Could the Cabinet Minister expand on how the agency will support businesses across the nation to grow, and outline the steps to ensure that a holistic approach is adopted to avoid that piecemeal system? Thank you.
contributions.text_original: Rwy'n siŵr bod pawb yn y Siambr hon eisiau gweld brand Cymru yn llwyddo. Er mwyn i hyn ddigwydd, mae angen inni helpu busnesau Cymreig i dyfu, arloesi a masnachu yn rhyngwladol, denu buddsoddiad mewnol, a chynyddu nifer y swyddi cynaliadwy o ansawdd da sy'n talu'n dda. Gwyddom fod y dirwedd fusnes flaenorol yn dameidiog ac yn aml yn ddryslyd, gan olygu na chafodd busnesau y gefnogaeth oedd ei hangen pan oedd ei hangen arnynt. Felly, mae croeso i'r cam o greu asiantaeth ddatblygu genedlaethol i Gymru fel canolfan un stop i gefnogi busnesau o bob maint ledled y wlad. A all y Gweinidog Cabinet ymhelaethu ar sut y bydd yr asiantaeth yn cefnogi busnesau ledled y wlad i dyfu, ac amlinellu'r camau i sicrhau y mabwysiadir dull cyfannol er mwyn osgoi system dameidiog? Diolch.

contributions.item_title_en: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Priorities for social care, mental health and women's health
contributions.text_english: I'm grateful to my colleagues for already mentioning the important issue of endometriosis. We know that delays in diagnosis and treatment can span years, whilst women are left in pain, struggling to work and facing long-term health consequences. Women are being failed by the gender pain gap, where they are more likely to experience chronic pain but are statistically more likely to have their symptoms dismissed. The Deputy Minister will be aware that I have recently written to her raising concerns regarding the future of Wales's only specialist endometriosis centre. The women's health plan recognises the need for improved pathways, specialist expertise and timely access to surgery. How will this Government support women across Wales, ensuring that patients across all health boards can access the level of care that they need to get their lives back?

I met with unpaid carers from across the county in Cimla recently, where a number of people highlighted the financial strain of providing that care. Do you agree with me, therefore, that, in order to better support unpaid carers in Wales, carers allowance should be devolved and increased in line with Scotland?

contributions.item_title_en: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
contributions.text_english: We know that the Government is committed to ensuring equitable access to cancer services across all parts of Wales, and I welcome that this new Plaid Cymru Government is placing a strong emphasis on this through its proposed cancer plan. Could the Cabinet Secretary therefore provide an update on progress towards establishing a rapid diagnosis centre in Powys? Diolch.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the First Minister
contributions.text_english: 9. How will the Government ensure that economic development supports both rural and urban areas? OQ64168
contributions.text_original: 9. Sut y bydd y Llywodraeth yn sicrhau bod datblygu economaidd yn cefnogi ardaloedd gwledig a threfol? OQ64168

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the First Minister
contributions.text_english: Thank you, First Minister. As a nation, we are regularly towards the bottom of economic tables after over 26 years of Labour Government. The need to improve and strengthen the Welsh economy is clear, and the Plaid Cymru economic plan and the ideas set out in the manifesto are very promising. But we must ensure that everyone in our country can benefit from these improvements and that our vision for the economy works for many sectors and communities. How will the Welsh Government ensure that our rural areas are not forgotten and that they do receive the support that they deserve? Thank you.
contributions.text_original: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Fel gwlad, rydym yn rheolaidd tuag at waelod y tablau economaidd ar ôl dros 26 mlynedd o Lywodraeth Llafur. Mae'r angen i wella a chryfhau economi Cymru yn amlwg, ac mae cynllun economaidd Plaid Cymru a'r syniadau yn y maniffesto yn addewidiol iawn. Ond mae'n rhaid sicrhau bod pawb yn ein gwlad yn medru buddio o'r gwellhad yma a bod ein gweledigaeth ar gyfer yr economi yn gweithio i amryw sectorau a chymunedau. Sut fydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn sicrhau nad yw ein hardaloedd gwledig yn cael eu hanghofio a'u bod yn derbyn y gefnogaeth maent yn ei haeddu? Diolch.

contributions.item_title_en: 6. Welsh Labour Debate: School support staff negotiating body
contributions.text_english:
I will have to declare an interest as a chair of governors and also because a close member of my family works as a member of support staff at a school.

The Unison Wales report, 'Time to value School Support Staff', sheds light on the situation that school support staff face across Wales. From being overworked and underpaid with term-time only pay, to limited opportunities to train and grow in the role, it's clear that support staff face a range of problems. We know of the challenging situation facing the education sector more broadly in Wales, from low Programme for International Student Assessment scores to absence issues.

I'm confident that Plaid Cymru can tackle these challenges. However, there is a need for a holistic approach. We can't help support staff by only tackling issues of pay, crucial as they are. We must also increase teacher recruitment and retention rates, expand free school meals to support pupils throughout their school careers, and reduce the workload for all educational staff. These are major issues, and major issues take time to resolve. The Government must ensure that it takes the right steps to tackle these matters facing our support staff. Rushing to a decision won't lead to meaningful, long-term support that will help with the real problems facing staff in the sector. Thank you.
contributions.text_original:
Bydd yn rhaid i fi ddatgan diddordeb fel cadeirydd llywodraethwyr a hefyd gan fod aelod agos o'r teulu yn gweithio fel staff cymorth ysgol.

Mae adroddiad Unison Cymru, 'Time to value School Support Staff', yn taflu golau ar y sefyllfa y mae staff cymorth ysgolion yn ei hwynebu ledled Cymru. O gael eu gorymestyn a’u tandalu gyda thâl tymor yn unig, i gyfleoedd hyfforddi cyfyngedig a diffyg lle i dyfu yn y rôl, mae'n amlwg bod staff cymorth yn wynebu ystod o broblemau. Gwyddom am gyflwr heriol y sector addysg yn ehangach yng Nghymru, o sgoriau Rhaglen Ryngwladol Asesu Myfyrwyr isel i broblemau absenoldebau.

Rwy'n hyderus y gall Plaid Cymru fynd i'r afael â’r heriau hyn. Fodd bynnag, mae angen dull holistig. Ni allwn helpu staff cefnogi wrth fynd i'r afael â materion cyflog yn unig, er mor hanfodol y maen nhw. Rhaid i ni hefyd gynyddu recriwtio a chadw athrawon, ehangu prydiau ysgol am ddim i gefnogi disgyblion trwy gydol eu bywyd ysgol, a lleihau llwyth gwaith i'r holl staff addysgu. Mae'r rhain yn faterion mawr, ac mae materion mawr yn cymryd amser i'w datrys. Rhaid i'r Llywodraeth wneud yn siŵr ei bod yn cymryd y camau cywir i fynd i'r afael â’r materion sy'n wynebu ein staff cymorth. Ni fydd rhuthro i benderfyniad yn arwain at gefnogaeth ystyrlon hir dymor a fydd yn helpu gyda phroblemau bywyd go iawn staff y sector. Diolch yn fawr.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the First Minister
contributions.text_english: Over recent weeks, concerns have been raised by residents in the Swansea valley regarding the condition of the River Tawe, following reports that a number of individuals, many children, have fallen ill after entering the water. I welcome the new Plaid Cymru Government's commitment to improve the collection and quality of data on pollution incidents, and its ambition to ensure that every water body in Wales achieves at least good ecological status. May I ask the First Minister to provide assurance to residents within my constituency of Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd that the Government will work closely with Natural Resources Wales and Dŵr Cymru to thoroughly investigate these incidents, and take the necessary action to safeguard public health and improve water quality? Diolch.
